brief: Goldman flows strategist Lee Coppersmith asks whether the equity panic (SPX below 7,000, GS Vol Panic Index at 9.8/10 Friday) is buyable. Base rate favors buying: across 42 episodes with the index at 9 or above, the S&P averaged +4.4% over the next three months, higher 78% of the time. Two caveats weaken that. First, the Fed is hiking, not cutting: in the five hiking-regime panic episodes, three-month returns averaged just +0.4% (versus +4.6% when the Fed was on hold and +5.4% when cutting), though a one-month bounce still held (+1.4%, up 80% of the time). Second, positioning is mixed: hedge funds have purged risk (net leverage to a five-year low, momentum flipped negative, VIP longs lagging badly), but mutual funds, ETFs and asset managers have not, with $170bn of Q4 inflows keeping Goldman's sentiment indicator at the 75th percentile, far from prior bottoms. Coppersmith calls this panic without the broad investor washout that historically marks lows, draws a Q4 2018 analog, and recommends selling puts rather than chasing stocks: a tactical bounce looks likely, but not a confirmed bottom.
